meta.travelSource: Door-to-door public transport times from S+U Alexanderplatz, read from the live VBB journey API on 4 September 2026 for a weekday morning departure. Final bus and walking legs are included.
meta.onSiteSource: Minimum sensible time on the ground is my own guide judgement, not an official figure.

centre.name: Stay in the centre
centre.line: U5 to Museumsinsel, three minutes from Alexanderplatz
centre.why: The one option where nothing can go wrong with the journey. Four hours buys one big collection at a human pace instead of three at a jog, plus the Lustgarten in between.
centre.watch: Most Museum Island houses are closed on Mondays, and the Pergamon Museum is still shut for its long rebuild.

options.name: Tempelhofer Feld
options.line: U5 then U6 to Paradestr., about 19 minutes
options.why: Two disused runways, 300 hectares of open sky and no ticket for anything. Walk one runway end to end, then drop into the Schillerkiez cafés on Herrfurthplatz.
options.watch: The field is fenced and gated. In September the gates open 06:30 and close 21:30; in October it is 07:00 to 19:00.

options.name: Charlottenburg
options.line: S-Bahn to Zoo or Wilmersdorfer Str., then U7 or bus M45, about 24 minutes
options.why: The other Berlin. A baroque palace with a garden that runs to the Spree, then Kurfürstendamm and the broken tower of the Memorial Church for contrast.
options.watch: Charlottenburg Palace is closed on Mondays. April to October it opens 10:00 to 17:30, last entry 30 minutes before. Old Palace 12 euros, charlottenburg+ for everything in the gardens 19 euros.

options.name: Köpenick
options.line: S3 to Köpenick in 25 minutes, then tram or a 10 minute walk to the old town
options.why: A small island old town where the Dahme meets the Spree, with a moated palace and a riverside that feels like a different federal state. This is the one guests never expect.
options.watch: Köpenick Palace is a museum with its own opening days, and the riverside restaurants get busy on warm weekends.

options.name: Wannsee and Peacock Island
options.line: S7 to Wannsee in 32 minutes, then bus 218 to the ferry in 10
options.why: Berlin's lake edge, and a two minute ferry to an island with a white folly palace, peacocks and no cars at all.
options.watch: The ferry runs 10:00 to 18:00 from March to October and the last crossing over is 45 minutes before that. Ferry ticket 6 euros, Peacock House 8 euros extra, bought on the day at the ferry house.

options.name: Sachsenhausen Memorial
options.line: S1 or RB32 to Oranienburg in about 45 minutes, then bus 804 for 7 minutes
options.why: The concentration camp north of the city, kept as a memorial and museum. It is the heaviest thing on this list and the one that changes how the rest of Berlin reads.
options.watch: Entry is free. Grounds and exhibitions open 08:30 to 18:00 until 26 October, then 08:30 to 16:30. Audio guide 3.50 euros. This is not a half-day you follow with dinner plans.

options.name: Potsdam and Sanssouci
options.line: S7 to Potsdam Hbf in 42 minutes, then a bus to Schloss Sanssouci in about 16
options.why: A whole royal park, a vineyard terrace, and a town centre worth an hour on its own. The single most popular day out from Berlin, and the one people most often try to squeeze.
options.watch: Sanssouci Palace is closed on Mondays, runs timed entry slots and sells a limited number of tickets a day, so book online. April to October 10:00 to 17:30. Palace ticket 14 euros, sanssouci+ for all the Potsdam palaces open that day 22 euros. You need an ABC transport ticket.

options.name: Spreewald
options.line: S5 to Ostbahnhof then RE2, about 65 minutes door to door
options.why: A landscape of small canals where the punt boats still do the work of roads. Nothing else on this list feels less like a city.
options.watch: The punt trips run on their own timetable and the classic loop takes two to three hours on the water, so an early train matters more here than anywhere else.
